outline_section.section_title: Introduction to RLC Circuit Differential Equation
outline_section.learning_goal: Orient the learner to a series RLC model and the target equation form $LC\,\frac{d^2 y(t)}{dt^2}+RC\,\frac{d y(t)}{dt}+y(t)=x(t)$ before any substitution-heavy algebra.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Schematic of a single-loop series RLC circuit with source input $x(t)$, resistor $R$, inductor $L$, capacitor $C$, and output $y(t)$ taken across the capacitor.
visual_elements: series source-loop with R, L, C symbols
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Minimal technical line drawing, no decorative styling. Clear node labels and current direction arrow in a single loop.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Show the direct move: apply one-loop KVL to a series RLC and connect element equations to create one differential equation in $y(t)$ and $x(t)$.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use a single series topology with $v_R$, $v_L$, $v_C$, same-current loop, and output on the capacitor.
paragraph_plan: Name input $x(t)$, output $y(t)=v_C(t)$, and define loop current $i(t)$ for all three passive elements.
State branch equations $v_R(t)=R i(t)$, $v_L(t)=L\,\frac{d i(t)}{dt}$, and $i(t)=C\,\frac{d y(t)}{dt}$.
Write one-loop KVL in symbolic form $x(t)=v_R(t)+v_L(t)+v_C(t)$ and show what substitution target it enables.
Preview coefficient interpretation: the resulting constant, first-derivative, and second-derivative multipliers become denominator coefficients for later pole work.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep this section strictly conceptual and short so the first worked example can start from the explicit KVL form without overloading cognitive load.

question_policy.practice_question_model: For a series RLC with $x(t)$ input and $y(t)$ output across the capacitor, choose the correct un-substituted KVL equation.
distractor_plan: Drop one of the three element voltages from the KVL sum.
Use subtraction or wrong sign on a voltage drop in the sum.
Write source equation as product of elements instead of sum.
Use current as output symbol in place of $y(t)$.
Omit dependence on time in $x(t)$ and $y(t)$.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Write the KVL equation for the shown series RLC circuit with input $x(t)$ and output $y(t)=v_C(t)$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce the explicit loop identity $x(t)=v_R(t)+v_L(t)+v_C(t)$ using the same current direction used in the diagram.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: The tutorial introduced the same diagram; this step applies it with formal KVL notation and explicit branch-sum structure.
solution_step_plan: Restate the loop and current direction from the diagram.
Write one KVL equation equating source voltage to the series sum of branch voltages.
Label each term with its associated component to prevent sign ambiguity.
practice_variation_axes: Change only variable symbols (for example, $x\to u$, $y\to v_C$)
Swap explicit naming of source/output while preserving topology

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep sign conventions identical to Tutorial image so later example and question stages do not need reinterpretation of direction.
